headline: Streamlined ESRS Finalised and Battery Passport Services Launch
summary: The EU has finalised streamlined European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS), simplifying compliance for your upcoming CSRD obligations. Meanwhile, battery passport certification services are launching, and proposed CBAM extensions to downstream products are heading to trilogue negotiations, threatening future import duties on finished goods.

items.title: Streamlined ESRS Finalised
items.what: The EU has finalised streamlined European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) alongside a new voluntary standard for non-listed entities.
items.meaning: As a listed brand within the CSRD scope from financial year 2027, these simplified standards will govern your sustainability disclosures.
items.action: Review the finalised standards to align your data collection systems before the 2027 financial year.

sources.title: EU Finalizes Streamlined ESRS and New Voluntary Reporting Standard
sources.origin: Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld LLP

sources.title: Europe is redefining the rules on sustainability reporting: new NEIS and a voluntary standard

items.title: Battery Passport Certification Launches
items.what: TÜV SÜD has launched a Digital Battery Passport certification service, while e-bike brands are actively partnering to deploy passports ahead of EU deadlines.
items.meaning: Your proprietary battery platform must comply with EU battery passport requirements. Third-party certification options are now becoming available.
items.action: Engage with certification bodies to pilot battery passports for your platform.

sources.title: TÜV SÜD launches Digital Battery Passport certification
Minespider and Tenways partner on e-bike battery passports ahead of EU regulation

items.title: CBAM Downstream Extension Progresses
items.what: Proposed amendments to extend the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) to downstream products and prevent circumvention are moving toward trilogue negotiations.
items.meaning: Although you currently import finished goods exempt from CBAM, a downstream extension could subject your imported power tools to carbon tariffs.
items.action: Monitor the trilogue negotiations and assess the carbon intensity of your suppliers' steel and aluminium.

sources.title: EU’s CBAM Downstream Extension and Anti-Circumvention Amendments: the Road to Trilogue

items.title: Right to Repair Italy Entry
items.what: Italy will bring the EU Right to Repair Directive into force on 22 October 2026. The EU also published an official corrigendum to the directive.
items.meaning: As the manufacturer under EU law, you must ensure your power tools and garden equipment sold in Italy comply with these repairability rules.
items.action: Verify that spare parts and repair information are accessible for the Italian market.

sources.title: Repair of goods: in Italia, the EU directive will come into force on 22 October

items.title: Greenwashing Ban in Force
items.what: The EU ban on vague environmental claims under the Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive officially took effect on 27 September 2026.
items.meaning: Generic green claims on your packaging or marketing materials are now prohibited unless backed by certified environmental performance.
items.action: Audit all consumer-facing sustainability claims on your products and website.
